title: When the Ferry Goes Your Way

plate.narration: At Ashspan Bridge, river water taps the ferry landing. A flat boat waits beside its long pole. The road crosses overhead, while the current carries on toward the coast.

goal.text: Get the travelers across the river, then help mend Ashspan Bridge.

steps.label: Get the new planks to the bridge

bridge.narration: Ashspan Bridge crosses the Great River here, but the melt has torn the planks out of its middle. Old Ossley, the frogfolk boatman, leans on the pole of his flat boat. "Folk cannot walk over, so they ride with me," he says. "Help me ferry them across. Then help me mend the bridge."

variants.text: He checks the blanket around your shoulders before he takes up his pole.

landing.narration: A mooring rope has dragged the landing plank loose. It wobbles like a loose tooth. Ossley holds the boat steady while two travelers wait with their bags. One bag quacks. How will you get them aboard?

plank_check.prompt: Hold the plank flat and still while the travelers step aboard.

rope_check.prompt: Flip the mooring rope off the plank before the boat drifts away.

brace_check.prompt: Brace the plank end like a post while the heavy bags cross.

plank.narration: You hold the plank flat until both travelers are aboard. Ossley tests it with his pole. "That will do." One traveler pats the plank, the way you pat a good horse.

rope.narration: You lift the rope clear, and the plank settles. The travelers board with dry bags. Ossley gives you a tiny nod. From a frogfolk boatman, that is a parade.

brace_done.narration: The plank end does not budge, even when the heaviest bag thumps across. Ossley taps it. "Like a post," he says. "A post that gets out of the way after. Hard to find."

board_wet.narration: The plank tips, and one bag drops into the shallows, quacking. Everyone fishes it out. "It floats," says its owner. "It is a very good bag." Ossley wrings out his hat and says nothing. That is how frogfolk laugh.

ferry_ask.narration: The nearer traveler hugs her bag. "I'm Tilly. Duck eggs, for market across the river. They are not due for days." The bag quacks. "They disagree." Ossley pushes off. "Strong river this year," he says. "A flat boat spins if the weight sits wrong."

ferry_plan.narration: Ossley hands out jobs. "The boat needs steadying, and the river needs watching. I only have two eyes, and one is on my hat." How will you help him across?

pole_check.prompt: Push the pole against the current beside Ossley, stroke after stroke.

watch_check.prompt: Fly above the water, spot the snags and call a safe line back to Ossley.

ferry_hold.prompt: Ossley calls the lean! Shift your weight together, then back, so the boat cannot spin.

crossing.narration: The flat boat wobbles like a duck, then slides across as straight as a plank. "Good," says Ossley. "Frogfolk dislike spinning." Tilly counts her eggs. It takes no time, since they are all in one bag.

ferry_spin.narration: The boat turns one slow circle. The bridge goes by twice. Ossley's throat puffs out like a drum. He jams his pole into the mud, and the boat stops, a little dizzy. Tilly checks her bag. "Still quacking."

ferry_dock.narration: The far landing comes up fast. "Bump, do not crash," says Ossley. "Tell me when." Tilly covers her bag with both hands.

interaction.cue: Tap when the boat swings level with the landing.

onSuccess.narration: A gentle bump. The boat stops, and the eggs do not even quack.

onFailure.narration: The boat hits the dock a little hard. The eggs quack. "Landed," says Ossley. "Mostly."

onAssisted.narration: Ossley eases the pole, and the boat slides in. He pretends it was you.

far_bank.narration: A dragonling bridge-mender named Bryn glares at the broken deck. "Planks, I have, in my cart up the bank. Hands, I do not. Help me fix this, and the market folk can cross." "And my eggs can get to market," says Tilly. A heap of old planks blocks the ramp.

plank_pile.narration: Bryn frowns at the heap. "That pile must move before my cart can come down. It has been there since dawn. I think it is breathing." The pile gives a small, damp sigh.

poke_reveal.narration: You poke the pile. It blinks. Eyes open under the top plank, then a wide wet mouth. They are two mire mimics, a big one and a little one. Mimics dress up as whatever lies on the ground and wait for a snack. Tilly's bag smells like duck.

stamp_reveal.narration: Thump, thump, thump! The whole pile jumps. A mouth opens under the top plank, and stubby legs unfold. They are two mire mimics, a big one and a little one. Mimics dress up as whatever lies on the ground and wait for a snack. Tilly's bag smells like duck.

mimic_fight.narration: The mire mimics wobble up, planks clattering down their backs. They want a snack, a nap and some peace, in that order. Shoo them back to the reeds before they eat Tilly's bag!

mimic_won.narration: The mimics hiccup, drop their planks and waddle off to the reeds. They leave behind a springy bootlace one of them once swallowed. "Not mine," says Bryn. "Yours." Ossley nods. "Hard to unload a pile that argues."

mimic_shooed.narration: The mimics are faster than they look. You end up in the mud with a plank on your head. Ossley tips both mimics into the reeds with his pole, then pours you warm tea from a flask.

cart_plan.narration: Bryn's cart of new planks sits in mud up to its axle. Her two pack goats pull and slip. One sits down, as if to say, call me when it is over. How will you free the cart?

dig_check.prompt: Dig the mud away from the wheel and push the cart free.

track_check.prompt: Work out where the old planks go so the wheel can climb out.

roar_check.prompt: Roar so the goats pull together, then steer the cart out straight.

cart_free.narration: The wheel pops free with a slurp. The goats trot up the bank as if it were their idea. Bryn kisses one on the nose, and it eats her sleeve. She hands you a brave whistle. "For calling goats. They ignore it, but it is very loud."

cart_stuck.narration: The mud wins, until Ossley's rope and everyone's backs haul the cart out. One plank snaps. "Kindling," sighs Bryn. She hands you a brave whistle. "For calling goats. They ignore it." The goats pretend to be someone else's goats.

unload_relay.narration: The cart cannot cross the broken end, so the planks go by hand. Everyone makes a line down to Bryn. One goat watches, no help at all.

interaction.cue: Catch a plank, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Plank after plank goes hand to hand, tap, tap, tap, all the way to the bridge.

onFailure.narration: A plank slips into the mud with a splat. Bryn scrapes it clean, but it is cracked.

onAssisted.narration: Bryn takes the middle, and the planks fly down the line like loaves at a bakery.

bridge_head.narration: The planks are stacked at the bridge end. Below, logs and branches have jammed against the first stone pier. "The river threw its furniture at us," says Bryn. If the heap shifts, it will shove the bridge crooked.

jam_plan.narration: The jam is logs, roots and one whole fence. Ossley squints at it. "Pull the wrong log, and the rest may roll." What will you do?

hook_check.prompt: Hook each log with the long pole and pull it clear of the pier.

haul_check.prompt: Grab the rope. Pull the whole heap loose on Ossley's call!

slip_check.prompt: Slip along the pier, find the key log and pull it out clean.

jam_shift.narration: The heap lurches, and the pier shudders. A plank slides off the stack and splashes in. Ossley hooks it back with his pole. "Rude," he tells the river. The river does not say sorry.

jam_clear.narration: The last log slides free and bobs away. Then one log floats back upriver, against the current, before it turns and follows the rest. "Changed melt," Ossley says quietly. The pier stands straight. Above it waits the cracked middle beam.

carry_beam.narration: The new beam lies on the bank, thick as a sleeping cow. Everyone takes a place along it. Bryn walks backward in front, calling, "Level! Level! Mostly level!"

interaction.cue: Lift or lower your end until the beam rides level in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: The beam rides level all the way, like a very long, very serious tray.

onFailure.narration: The beam tips and bonks a goat on the rump. The goat is more surprised than hurt. You go again, slower.

onAssisted.narration: Bryn takes the middle, and the beam rides level the whole way.

beam_plan.narration: The new beam must go up into its notches, level, with nobody underneath. How will you raise it?

lift_check.prompt: Grab the beam. Lift together when Ossley counts three!

roll_check.prompt: Set the log rollers and the slope so the beam rolls up, not sideways.

smash_check.prompt: Smash the cracked beam loose, then slide the new one into the notches.

hum_check.prompt: Hum a steady count so everyone lifts at once, and keep the beam level.

beam_up.narration: The beam drops into its notches with a deep thunk. Bryn pats it like a pony. "Do not tell the old one." Ossley taps it, and it rings clear. Bryn hands around her lunch pail: a supper bundle, still warm.

beam_slip.narration: The beam thumps in a finger crooked and scrapes everyone's hands. Bryn taps it straight with a mallet. "It was shy. Now it is brave." It rings a bit flat, but it rings. Bryn hands around her lunch pail: a supper bundle, still warm.

hatch.narration: Tilly's bag cracks. A tiny beak pokes out. "Oh no," says Tilly. "Oh yes," says Ossley. A duckling the size of a teacup tumbles out, then a whole fluffy handful. They waddle toward the gap in the deck, peeping.

duck_play.narration: The ducklings peep in circles around everyone's boots, far too excited to listen.

interaction.cue: Everyone, settle the ducklings with something gentle.

options.label: Scatter oat crumbs
options.reaction: The ducklings tumble after the crumbs in a fluffy rush.

options.label: Pet a soft little head
options.reaction: A duckling leans into your hand and closes its eyes.

options.label: Hum a slow tune
options.reaction: The peeping slows down to match your humming.

onSuccess.narration: The ducklings settle into one warm heap, yawning.

onFailure.narration: A few keep peeping, but they stay close to your boots.

onAssisted.narration: Tilly tucks the ducklings into her hat, and they quiet down at once.

duck_plan.narration: One duckling wanders to the edge and peers down at the water with great interest. "Eggs," says Tilly faintly, "are supposed to wait until market." She holds out an empty basket. How will you get them to safety?

scoop_check.prompt: Sweep the ducklings into Tilly's basket before they reach the gap.

coax_check.prompt: Crouch low and call softly until the ducklings follow you.

trail_check.prompt: Draw a bright trail through the air and lead the ducklings into the basket.

ducks_safe.narration: The ducklings tumble into the basket and go quiet. Tilly counts, loses count and counts again. "All of them!" One falls asleep on Ossley's hat, and he does not dare move. Tilly ties a songbird ribbon around your wrist. "For my heroes."

ducks_loose.narration: Three ducklings dash for the gap and cling to a plank end, peeping. Ossley fishes them out with his net. One pecks your ankle. Tilly tucks them all in the basket. "They will learn. In about a year." She ties a songbird ribbon around your wrist.

planks_plan.narration: Now the deck. Bryn's planks wait at the bridge end, and the gap yawns between the two halves. How will you get the planks across?

rope2_check.prompt: Slide each plank along the rope line, tap it in, and send the next.

pass_check.prompt: Pass each plank hand to hand, and keep a steady rhythm going.

pwing_check.prompt: Fly the line across the gap and land every plank square.

planks_dropped.narration: A plank slips off and slaps into the river. Ossley drags it back with his pole, grumbling about wet wood. Bryn wrings it out like laundry, and the deck gets laid anyway.

planks_laid.narration: The planks go down, tap, tap, tap, until one hole is left, about the size of a goat. Bryn fits the last plank. "Now we tie it down." A goat eyes the hole and slowly walks away.

variants.text: One plank was lost in the mud, so Ossley gives up a spare board from his boat, sniffing.

lash_plan.narration: Bryn taps a loose plank. "A deck only stays if it is tied down." The ropes wait in a coil, the pegs in a bucket. How will you fasten the deck?

knots_check.narration: You tie each plank end to the beams. Bryn checks every knot and tugs it twice.

pegs_check.narration: You drive in the pegs while Bryn holds the planks square. Bonk, bonk, bonk.

whistle_check.narration: The whistle brings the goats, for once. Ossley hitches them to the line, and together you walk it tight.

straps_check.narration: Your duskrunner darts along the deck, cinching straps while friends hold the loose ends.

lashed.narration: The last knot snaps tight, and the deck stops creaking. Bryn struts along it like a cat that owns the place. "A bridge must carry everyone at once," she says. "Everyone on the deck. Ossley too." Ossley sighs and hops up.

test_check.narration: You walk the deck with Bryn, plank by plank. Nothing wobbles. "Fastenings first," she says. "Then I call the travelers."

bridge_open.narration: Every plank holds. Bryn does a small dance, then pretends she did not. At the far end, the market folk start across in a long, chattering line, baskets on their heads.

folk_cross.narration: Tilly crosses last with her peeping ducklings. "I would have missed market," she tells Ossley. "Thank you." He tips his hat, then checks it for ducks. Bryn pays you six coins from the toll box. "A bridge pays its menders."

gift_plan.narration: Tilly rummages in her feathery bag. "I must give you something. I have oat cakes, and a story about a goose. The cakes are better. The story is longer."

buy_cakes.narration: Tilly takes your three coins very seriously. She gives one back for luck, then takes it back. "Business is business." The cakes are warm, and smell faintly of duckling.

cakes.narration: Tilly presses warm oat cakes into your hands. "Do not share them with ducks," she says. "They take advantage." A duckling peeps, as if accused.

goose.narration: Tilly tells the story of a goose who tried to marry a weathervane. It has three endings. Ossley falls asleep standing up. You like the goose very much, and the weathervane a little less.

rest_hut.narration: Bryn lights a stove in the bridge-house. It smells of oats, and a little of goat. Ossley points to a raised footpath into the Whispering Marsh. "A school called the Academy is up there. They made me a reed mat, and nobody has fetched it. Follow the posts. The ducks take shortcuts. You should not."

share_bryn.narration: You set out your supper. Bryn adds oats, and Ossley adds a fish nobody asked about. It is an odd meal and a very good one. Bryn hangs a river charm around your neck. "It keeps the wet out of your boots. Mostly."

dangle.narration: The deck is warm from the sun. Ossley sits beside you and names seven fish he has argued with. The worst is called Gerald. Gerald always wins.

tie_boat.narration: Ossley shows you his favorite knot, the one that comes undone when he whistles. You practice until it comes undone when you whistle. "A natural," he says, "or a menace."

ossley_routes.narration: Ossley coils his rope. "Tomorrow's tide takes me downriver, to the coast called the Saltrot." He points up the road. "Or there are the old boundary stones, where the keepers count things. Ask me about one."

coast_talk.narration: "Salt flats and silt," says Ossley. "This year the silt came from somewhere I do not know. I will take whoever wants to come. I am generally going your way." He looks at his hat. "Sometimes the river agrees."

inland_talk.narration: "The keepers count old stones," says Ossley. "They ask the river questions, and it never answers in the same order. Ask nicely. Bring a cheese." He blinks both eyelids at once. That means a joke.

routes.narration: The bridge is whole, and the landing is safe. Ossley points downriver to the Saltrot and up the road to the boundary stones. Then he marks the upper bank road north to Frostfang Shore. "Long walk. Griffin country at the end." Whichever way you go, he is generally going it too.

marsh_path.narration: The raised path carries you into the Whispering Marsh. Ahead stands a village on wooden legs. A rolled reed mat waits by a sign: "For the ferry. Please keep dry." A puddle covers the last stretch. How will you carry the mat?

mat_high.narration: You carry the mat overhead to a dry bench in the village. A duck walks under it. For a moment, the duck has a roof.

mat_wrap.narration: You wrap the mat in a dry cloak and carry it to a bench in the village. The mat stays dry. Your socks do not.

village_rest.narration: You rest by the dry mat. A round tower rises above the reeds. It has no roof. A page of homework floats down and lands on a duck. The duck looks proud of its marks.

mat_return.narration: You follow the posts back to the bridge. Ossley unrolls the dry mat across his wet deck. The travelers step on without slipping. "Better," he says.

academy.narration: At the top of the tower above the marsh village is a classroom with no roof. This school is called the Academy. Here you can learn to be a Starweaver, a hero who reads the stars. A dragonling named Professor Nettle stands by a huge brass telescope while homework drifts off the desks. A star circlet rests on a cushion. A Starweaver's light lives in it, and a dusk hood worn beside it starts to itch. "Anyone may try it on," says the professor.

variants.text: Professor Nettle waves from the brass telescope. "Back at the Academy! Mind the homework." The star circlet waits on its cushion.

academy_stars.narration: Professor Nettle lets you look through the telescope. Even by day, the stars look close enough to count their points. Then the telescope sneezes. Dust puffs out. "Bless you," says the professor. "It does that when it sees something new."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
